tiers.core: Pinned by the kit as a git submodule under .claude/skills/ext/ and installed by default.
tiers.extension: Pinned by the kit the same way and installed on demand: bash .claude/bin/skills.sh add <id>. An entry with a skills list is not a submodule: skills.sh fetches those folders from its source into .claude/skills/<name>/.
tiers.add-on: Entries without a tier are opt-in tools the kit does not pin. Install one only when the user asks.

commit: Every core and extension entry records the commit it is pinned at: for a submodule, the gitlink validate.sh checks the entry against; for a skills-list pack, the commit skills.sh fetches and asserts against FETCH_HEAD. bash .claude/bin/skills.sh pins rechecks them, --write rewrites them from the gitlinks.
triggers: Display text: the INSTALL WHEN column of skills.sh list, for people and agents choosing a pack. Nothing matches on it.
scope: Skill packs, plugins, template repos and catalogs — things an installer can put on disk. MCP servers are not listed here and never were installable from here: skills.sh writes no .mcp.json and runs no claude mcp add. A default server lives in .mcp.json; an opt-in one is a line in .claude/commands/setup-mcp.md that the user runs.

entries.name: Solana Fuzz Skill
entries.description: The Trident harness API at a pinned version, plus the flag that makes a fuzz run mean anything. Two things the kit does not already have: the v0.12.0 call surface written out (#[flow_executor], #[init]/#[flow]/#[end], process_transaction, get_account_with_type and its discriminator offset, PDA seeds in fuzz_accounts) so an agent stops authoring Trident calls from memory against an API that moves every minor version; and the --with-exit-code trap, where a failing invariant is swallowed in parallel mode and the run still exits 0, so a green CI job proves nothing. No other pinned pack mentions that flag, and /test-rust and /audit-solana both print trident fuzz run without it. It layers under auditor-skill rather than overlapping: that pack already calls Trident the default primary harness and ships 19 invariants phrased as Trident post-conditions, deciding what to assert; this one is how to build the harness that asserts it. Ships one runnable Anchor example that goes red on a planted wrapping_sub bug and green on the fix, pins Trident 0.12.0 stable over the 0.13 RC, and marks its own regression and trident compare surface as unverified.
entries.safety: clean; no env keys, no nested submodules, and it only writes test code. The Trident CLI it drives is a separate cargo install trident-cli --locked, and a fuzz run builds and executes the program under test, so run it on code you intend to build. Pinned pre-fix: the worked example still pins anchor-lang 0.31 and uses the pre-1.0 space = 8 + INIT_SPACE form (belumume/solana-fuzz#1, fix open in #2). That is the example program only -- the harness API this pack is pinned for is unaffected, since trident-tests/ depends on borsh and trident-fuzz and not on anchor-lang.

entries.name: Get Shit Pretty (GSP)
entries.description: Design engineering for a dApp's surface: a brand pipeline (strategy, identity, guidelines) and a project pipeline (brief, research, design, critique, build, review) across 45 skills and 13 scoped sub-agents, emitting shadcn registry themes, Tailwind tokens, a STYLE.md and WCAG 2.2 audits. 35 style presets. Not Solana-specific — it designs the client, not the program.
triggers: brand identity or a design system for the app
entries.safety: clean at this pin on every checklist item, verified across all 1,657 blobs in its history and not just the checkout: no eval, atob, new Function or createRequire; no install lifecycle hook in package.json, ever; zero occurrences of keypair, wallet, private-key, mnemonic or credential terms anywhere in the repo; no invisible or bidi Unicode; no whitespace-padded line; no base64 payload; every long line is prose or a Tailwind class string. Zero production dependencies. child_process appears in two statusline scripts only, argv-form with fixed arguments, and bin/install.js uses none. Its only egress is `npm view get-shit-pretty version` once per 24h, and the only IP literal is 127.0.0.1 in a loopback preset server that self-exits after 60s. Pinning it is inert: the kit copies ext/ packs as plain files, fetches no pack submodules and never reads a pack's .mcp.json or hooks.json, so neither takes effect in a session. Three things to know before wiring any of it by hand. (1) Its root .mcp.json declares a local stdio MCP server, `npx -y @anthropic/mcp-figma` carrying FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN, and that package does not exist: the whole @anthropic npm scope is unclaimed (Anthropic's is @anthropic-ai), so the name is squattable and a local MCP server runs outside the OS sandbox. Do not copy that file to a project root. (2) gsp/hooks/hooks.json wires PreToolUse on every Edit/Write, SessionStart on compact and twelve SubagentStop matchers to bash scripts/*.sh; those scripts are local, read-only over .design/ and parse stdin with jq, but they run unattended once wired. (3) dev/scripts/token-proxy.py is a mitmproxy addon that intercepts api.anthropic.com to count tokens; it records only usage counters to a local jsonl, transmits nothing, and needs both mitmproxy and an HTTPS_PROXY you set yourself. Correcting the earlier add-on note: bin/install.js does not merge hooks into settings.json — it writes settings.statusLine only and never references hooks.json or .mcp.json, so the pack's own installer does not wire its hooks either, despite its README advertising them. Its install.sh is stale (it copies commands/ and agents/ paths that no longer exist, under set -e) and targets ~/.claude globally; nothing in the kit runs it. A pin vendors the author's whole monorepo, ~4.6 MB over 571 files, of which the gsp/ payload is 1.6 MB and the rest is their marketing site, their own .design artifacts, dev tooling and nine commercial Pangram Pangram woff2 fonts. In --agents installs Codex and opencode load all 45 nested SKILL.md files.

The supabase-postgres-best-practices skill is a 34-file Postgres reference that holds for Postgres anywhere: query performance and EXPLAIN plans, connection pooling and exhaustion, partitioning, RLS policy performance, missing foreign-key indexes, and SKIP LOCKED queue patterns — the one to read when a Solana indexer or webhook consumer is writing high-volume rows.

A new Function does exist on the unmerged feature/workflow-evals branch, which the pin does not reach. entries.safety: Scanned at 9906a34 (2026-06-23): no lines over 500 characters, no eval, atob, new Function or createRequire, no bidi or invisible Unicode, no IP literals, no package.json and so no install lifecycle hook, no hooks.json, no .mcp.json and no .claude/settings.json; all 291 blobs across its 31 commits hold nothing the checkout does not, and nothing has ever been deleted from it. It ships two things that fire only if you install it as a Claude Code plugin, never at this ext/ pin: hooks/hooks.json runs node skills/expo-skill-feedback/scripts/skill-event.cjs on PostToolUse with matcher Skill and on UserPromptExpansion, and .mcp.json declares a remote HTTP MCP server at https://mcp.expo.dev/mcp, which names no npm package and so carries no dependency-confusion surface, though enabling it does send your Expo and EAS queries to Expo. Telemetry verified by reading telemetry_common.cjs and skill-event.cjs rather than taking the README's word: it is opt-in with DEFAULT_ON set to false and sends nothing until you create the marker file at ~/.expo-skills/opt-in or set EXPO_SKILLS_TELEMETRY=1; DO_NOT_TRACK=1 forces it off with the highest precedence; CI detection forces it off too, covering CI plus GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, CIRCLECI, TRAVIS, BUILDKITE, JENKINS_URL, TEAMCITY_VERSION and TF_BUILD. No prompt text, no file paths, no project or repository names. The phc_ PostHog key committed in that file is a write-only public ingestion key, documented as such in place. Ten executables, none of them reached by a published skill: eight are its own eval harness under .claude/skills/expo-skill-eval/scripts/, which boot simulators and run bunx expo, and scripts/ci.sh plus ci.py are its CI, where EVAL_HARNESS_ACCESS_TOKEN clones a private harness. entries.name: Solana Airdrop (Merkle distribution)
entries.description: Merkle-tree airdrops: recipient ingestion, root and per-recipient proofs, claim-instruction building for the Solana Foundation template and Metaplex gumdrop, anti-double-claim PDA derivation, anti-sybil eligibility patterns. A zero-dependency pure-Python Keccak-256 engine plus a TypeScript claim builder.

install.command: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/yusizer/solana-airdrop-skill && cd solana-airdrop-skill && bash install.sh .

entries.safety: no malware: scanned at 1b708843cd8104e3dd4433a0e85a6b443ed4c711 — no eval, atob or createRequire, no network egress, no keypair reads, stdlib-only Python. Its Keccak-256 is correct (cross-checked against SHA3 over 305 input lengths). Correctness caveats, though, and they matter because airdrop roots are irreversible: verify_all() is self-referential and cannot fail, so it does not catch a wrong leaf encoding, and its eval grades itself against its own root. De-dup keys on (pubkey, amount) while the Foundation template's claim PDA is per-claimant, so a repeated pubkey strands funds. The claim builder asks for a Keypair where a PublicKey would do, and its install.sh overwrites a project's agents, commands and rules without asking. See upstream issue 1; treat its gate as a self-consistency check and verify a root against the target program's own tooling before publishing
